title: Give each call its own environment
prompt:
Here is a toy term language with numbers, params, Add and Call(body, args). ev(env, t) works out the value of t. env is the environment of the call that is running: a list where env[i] is the value in slot i.

Three cases are right. The Call case is wrong: it runs the body with the caller's env, so the args are never used. Repair it in two moves. Work out each arg with the caller's env. Then run the body with a new environment made of those values.
hints: The body must not see the caller's `env`. It should see a list built from the args.
Each arg is a term, so work it out first, with the caller's `env`: `[ev(env, x) for x in args]`.
The whole case is `return ev([ev(env, x) for x in args], body)`. The args use the old environment and the body uses the new one.
explain: A call works out its args in the caller's environment, then runs the body in a new environment that holds only those values. The body's `Param(0)` now means the first arg of this call. Running the body with the caller's `env` gives 101 for the second sample, because the body would read the caller's slot 0.
